gen-dafont-eraser-gf-gowun-batang: Understated, Eraser makes an o with sides and top equally thick. Gowun Batang, with terminals cut back to leave a wide gap, gives that blocky lettering a literary counterpart below.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-habibi: Habibi brings traditional, editorial manners, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. But Eraser commands, its bold lines gliding under the eye like wire, while Habibi handles the steady reading.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-inika: Bold, unshaded outlines with no swelling define Eraser. Inika, classic and traditional, leaves a visible gap in each s, so beside Eraser's blunt weight it feels warmer and older.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-kay-pho-du: Eraser's bold letters never thicken or thin, one flat, confident stroke throughout. And Kay Pho Du lets its counters breathe like a hollow reed cut open, so the real strength here is heavy meeting light.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-labrada: Eraser gives its horizontal bars the same weight as its upright stems, so every bold letter looks cut from one block. Labrada keeps paragraphs dignified and unhurried, thanks to wide openings on its small letters.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-laila: Laila leaves generous space between its curve ends and the stem, an editorial, traditional habit. But Eraser keeps to a bold line with the steadiness of a technical pen, never swelling.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-montaga: Montaga reads bookish and editorial, its pen-lifted curves leaving each loop unfinished like thread stitched along a path. Eraser earns its keep big and short, in bold, unvarying strokes.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-new-tegomin: Commanding without any fuss, Eraser lays down bold letters with no thicker or thinner strokes. New Tegomin, whose c looks like a wide-open ring, keeps long reading dignified, traditional and unhurried.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-podkova: Eraser holds its line at an unvarying thickness, bold from every angle. And Podkova, with a broad, welcoming c, supplies what the pair does best: a bookish, traditional counterweight.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-rhodium-libre: Eraser draws a constant-width line, like a marker, in bold letters. And Rhodium Libre, with brush ends lifted away before the curve closes, brings an editorial, traditional counterpoint to the page.
